content.text:
PLAN AND DO STAGE 1:

FrostCore Stage 1 — "Allocator & Lifecycle Foundation"
Since quickjs-ng is a living C codebase, Stage 1 isn't rewriting — it's establishing the extraction boundary. You fork, you build, you inject control points.
Core Tasks
Table
#	Task	What It Means
1	Fork & Branch	Mirror quickjs-ng as upstream branch. All work happens on frostcore branch. Document rebase strategy for pulling upstream fixes.
2	Build System Migration	Replace whatever build quickjs-ng uses (likely meson or their own make) with your Makefile + build.sh/build.ps1. Must produce libfrostcore.a and frostcore.h cleanly.
3	Allocator Injection	Audit every malloc/free/realloc in the engine. Route them through function pointers stored in JSRuntime (or your wrapper struct). GlacioJS must be able to pass: alloc_fn, free_fn, realloc_fn, plus an opaque userdata pointer.
4	Explicit Lifecycle API	C wrapper around runtime creation/destruction: frost_runtime_create(), frost_runtime_destroy(). No hidden globals. Multiple runtimes must coexist without cross-contamination.
5	Minimal Eval Hook	frost_eval(runtime, source) — just enough JS execution surface for GlacioJS to test the handoff. No stdlib modules yet, just raw expression evaluation.
6	Smoke Test	Create 3+ runtimes simultaneously with different allocator configs, eval something, destroy them. Prove isolation works.
Deliverables
plain
Copy

libfrostcore.a          // Static library
include/frostcore.h     // Public C API (GlacioJS includes this)
Makefile
build.sh / build.ps1

The C API Surface (Stage 1)
c
Copy

typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void* (*alloc)(size_t size, void* userdata);
    void  (*free)(void* ptr, void* userdata);
    void* (*realloc)(void* ptr, size_t size, void* userdata);
    void* userdata;  // per-isolate arena, tracing hooks, etc.
} frost_alloc;

typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

frost_runtime* frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc* alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime* rt);

// Minimal eval for integration testing
int frost_eval(frost_runtime* rt, const char* source, char** out_error);

Explicitly NOT in Stage 1

    ❌ Parser/bytecode modularity (still one compilation unit)
    ❌ GC algorithm changes (keep quickjs-ng's ref-count + cycle GC)
    ❌ Stdlib separation (console, setTimeout, etc. still baked in or disabled, not modularized)
    ❌ C++ wrapper (pure C boundary)
    ❌ Task/isolate scheduler (that's GlacioJS Layer 2 using FrostCore runtimes)
    ❌ ES module loader hooks

$(QJS): $(BUILD_DIR)

	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) api-test.c

	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) gen/standalone.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) gen/test_fib.c
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) qjs.c

	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) quickjs-libc.c

	$(RUN262) -m -c test262.conf -E -a

/*
 * FrostCore — Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JS engine boundary
 * Public C API (Stage 1: Lifecycle + Eval)
 *
 * GlacioJS includes only this header; never includes quickjs.h directly.
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_H
#define FROSTCORE_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Allocator vtable
 *
 * Pass a filled frost_alloc to frost_runtime_create(). Every allocation
 * made by the runtime (including the GC heap) routes through these
 * pointers. userdata is forwarded opaquely on every call — use it for
 * per-isolate arenas, tracing hooks, capacity accounting, etc.
 *
 * calloc is optional: if NULL, the runtime falls back to alloc+memset.
 * malloc_usable_size is optional: if NULL, exact sizes are used instead
 * of the OS slab size, which is slightly less efficient.
 *
 * If alloc is NULL altogether, frost_runtime_create() uses the default
 * system allocator (equivalent to passing malloc/free/realloc).
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr); /* no userdata — POSIX convention */
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Runtime handle — opaque
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Lifecycle
 *
 * frost_runtime_create — alloc may be NULL to use the system allocator.
 *   Returns NULL on allocation failure.
 *
 * frost_runtime_destroy — frees everything owned by this runtime.
 *   Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.
 *
 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Minimal eval surface (integration handshake for GlacioJS)
 *
 * Evaluates `source` as a JS global script expression.
 * Returns  0 on success.
 * Returns -1 on error; *out_error receives a malloc'd (system malloc)
 *   NUL-terminated UTF-8 message — caller must free() it.
 *   out_error may be NULL if the caller doesn't want the message.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_H */

project(frostcore LANGUAGES C)

set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 11)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build quickjs-ng as a static library from the parent source tree.
# We compile only the engine files — no CLI, no libc module.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
set(QJS_ROOT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/..")

set(QJS_SOURCES
    "${QJS_ROOT}/quickjs.c"
    "${QJS_ROOT}/libregexp.c"
    "${QJS_ROOT}/libunicode.c"
    "${QJS_ROOT}/dtoa.c"
)

add_library(quickjs_static STATIC ${QJS_SOURCES})

target_include_directories(quickjs_static PUBLIC "${QJS_ROOT}")

target_compile_definitions(quickjs_static PRIVATE
    _GNU_SOURCE
    CONFIG_VERSION="frostcore-stage1"
)

# Suppress upstream warnings we don't control
if(CMAKE_C_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang|GNU")
    target_compile_options(quickjs_static PRIVATE
        -Wno-unused-parameter
        -Wno-sign-compare
        -Wno-missing-field-initializers
    )
endif()

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_library(frostcore STATIC src/frostcore.c)

)

target_compile_definitions(frostcore PRIVATE _GNU_SOURCE)

target_link_libraries(frostcore PUBLIC quickjs_static)

    target_link_libraries(frostcore PUBLIC m)

---
name: project-overview
description: FrostCore project purpose, architecture, and relationship to GlacioJS
metadata:
  type: project
---

FrostCore is a custom JS engine layer built on top of quickjs-ng. It is NOT a rewrite — it establishes an extraction boundary over the living quickjs-ng C codebase.

**Why:** GlacioJS (Layer 2 scheduler/isolate manager) needs a pluggable allocator, explicit multi-runtime lifecycle, and no hidden globals — none of which quickjs-ng's public API exposes cleanly enough. FrostCore adds that thin boundary.

**Architecture:**
- `frost/` — FrostCore overlay (never touches upstream quickjs-ng files)
- `frost/include/frostcore.h` — the ONLY header GlacioJS may include
- `frost/src/frostcore.c` — adapter/wrapper implementation
- `frost/tests/` — isolation smoke tests
- `frost/CMakeLists.txt` — builds `frostcore.lib` + `quickjs_static.lib`
- `build.sh` / `build.ps1` — end-to-end build + test scripts

**How to apply:** All GlacioJS integration goes through `frostcore.h`; never let GlacioJS import `quickjs.h` directly.

Planned stages: Stage 1 (done) → Stage 2: GlacioJS isolate scheduler → Stage 3: stdlib separation → Stage 4: bytecode modularity.

input.content:
# FrostCore

**Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JavaScript engine boundary layer.**

FrostCore wraps [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) with a thin C API that gives the embedding layer — GlacioJS — explicit control over memory allocation, runtime lifecycle, and JS evaluation. It is not a rewrite of the engine; it is an extraction boundary on top of a living upstream codebase.

---

## What FrostCore Is

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Per-runtime pluggable allocator | Stage 1 |
| Explicit `create` / `destroy` lifecycle (no hidden globals) | Stage 1 |
| Multiple runtimes coexisting in one process | Stage 1 |
| Minimal `eval` surface for integration testing | Stage 1 |
| GC algorithm changes | Not in scope |
| Parser/bytecode modularization | Stage 3+ |
| Stdlib separation | Stage 3+ |
| C++ wrapper | Not in scope |
| Task/isolate scheduler | GlacioJS Layer 2 |

---

## Repository Layout

```
FrostCore/
  quickjs.c / quickjs.h    — upstream quickjs-ng engine (do not edit)
  libregexp.c / libunicode.c / dtoa.c — upstream support files
  CMakeLists.txt / meson.build        — upstream build (untouched)
  README.txt                          — original quickjs-ng README

  frost/                   — FrostCore overlay (all Stage 1 work lives here)
    include/frostcore.h    — public C API — the ONLY header GlacioJS imports
    src/frostcore.c        — implementation
    tests/smoke_test.c     — isolation + leak smoke test
    Makefile               — builds libfrostcore.a without CMake

  build.sh                 — Unix: build + run smoke test
  build.ps1                — Windows: build + run smoke test
```

---

## Public API (Stage 1)

```c
#include "frostcore.h"

/* Allocator vtable — all fields except alloc/free/realloc are optional */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr);
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* Pass NULL to use the system allocator */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
   *out_error is malloc'd — caller must free() it. */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);
```

---

## Building

### Unix (clang required)

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh          # Release
./build.sh Debug
```

Produces `frost/build/libfrostcore.a` and runs the smoke test.

### Windows (PowerShell, clang in PATH)

```powershell
.\build.ps1
.\build.ps1 -BuildType Debug
```

Produces `frost\build\frostcore.lib` and runs the smoke test.

### Manual (from `frost/`)

```sh
make              # builds libfrostcore.a + smoke test, runs test
make lib          # libfrostcore.a only
make clean
```

---

## Smoke Test Output (Stage 1)

```
FrostCore Stage 1 — Smoke Test
================================
[rt_sys]   Creating runtime with system allocator...
[rt_count] Creating runtime with counting allocator...
[rt_sys2]  Creating second system-allocator runtime...

All three runtimes created successfully.

--- Eval tests ---
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval(1 + 1) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval(Math.sqrt(144)) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval('hello' + ' world') => ok
  PASS [rt_count]: eval(42 * 2) => ok
  PASS [rt_count]: eval(typeof undefined) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys2]:  eval(true || false) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys2]:  eval([1,2,3].length) => ok

--- Error handling ---
  PASS [rt_sys/syntax]:  SyntaxError: expecting ';'
  PASS [rt_count/ref]:   ReferenceError: undeclaredVariable is not defined
  PASS [rt_sys2/throw]:  Error: boom

--- Isolation test ---
  PASS [isolation]: __SENTINEL__ not visible in rt_sys2

--- Allocator accounting ---
  rt_count stats after destroy: allocs=1246, frees=1246   ← zero leaks

================================
All smoke tests PASSED.
```

---

## Upstream

FrostCore is built on [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) (MIT).
The original quickjs-ng README is preserved in [README.txt](README.txt).

Upstream sync strategy: `master` tracks `quickjs-ng/master`. All FrostCore work lives in `frost/` and never modifies upstream files, making rebases clean.

# FrostCore Stage 1 — Build System
# Produces: build/libfrostcore.a  build/frost_smoke[.exe]
#
# Usage:
#   make              — build lib + smoke test, run test
#   make lib          — libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         — build everything, run smoke test
#   make clean        — remove build/
#
# Variables (override on command line):
#   CC      — C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      — archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   — output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     — optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

# Source root is the parent of this Makefile (the repo root)
ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage1\"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c

FROST_SRCS := src/frostcore.c

SMOKE_SRCS := tests/smoke_test.c

# Object files land in build/
QJS_OBJS   := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))

LIB        := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke

# Detect Windows (MSYS/Git Bash / native) and add .exe suffix
ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    # msvcrt doesn't have -lm but it doesn't need it either
    LDLIBS    :=
else
    LDLIBS    := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)

# Smoke test binary
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# FrostCore static library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure build dir exists before any .o is built
$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (include path: repo root)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# frostcore wrapper object
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# smoke test object
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

    # msvcrt doesn't have -lm but it doesn't need it either
    LDLIBS    :=
else
    LDLIBS    := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)

# Smoke test binary
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# FrostCore static library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure build dir exists before any .o is built
$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (include path: repo root)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# frostcore wrapper object
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# smoke test object
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

---

## Stage 1 — Done

**Files created:**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [frost/include/frostcore.h](frost/include/frostcore.h) | Public C API — only header GlacioJS needs |
| [frost/src/frostcore.c](frost/src/frostcore.c) | Thin wrapper: allocator thunks + lifecycle + eval |
| [frost/tests/smoke_test.c](frost/tests/smoke_test.c) | 3-runtime isolation + leak test |
| [frost/Makefile](frost/Makefile) | Direct clang + llvm-ar build, no CMake |
| [build.sh](build.sh) | Unix wrapper |
| [build.ps1](build.ps1) | Windows PowerShell wrapper |
| [README.md](README.md) | FrostCore README (upstream moved to README.txt) |

**Smoke test results (verified on clang 21, Windows):**
- 3 runtimes created simultaneously with different allocator configs
- 7 eval expressions pass across all runtimes
- 3 error cases (syntax, reference, throw) return `-1` + correct message
- Isolation confirmed: `__SENTINEL__` set in `rt_sys` → `ReferenceError` in `rt_sys2`
- Counting allocator: `allocs=1246, frees=1246` — zero leaks through full lifecycle

**Key design note:** `JSMallocFunctions` already existed in quickjs-ng (`JS_NewRuntime2`). The `frost_alloc` vtable sits on top with a different arg order; static thunk functions bridge the two. No upstream file was modified.

**Git branch setup is deferred** — proceed when ready with `git remote rename origin upstream && git checkout -b frostcore`.

PLAN and DO STAGE 2, ALSO ADD TEST CASES TO IT

FrostCore Stage 2 — "Subsystem Split"
After allocator injection, the next cut is separating the engine from the stdlib. quickjs-ng bundles console, setTimeout, basic I/O, and utility objects into the runtime init. Stage 2 makes them optional.
Core Tasks
Table
#	Task	What It Means
1	Audit stdlib coupling	Find every JS_AddIntrinsic*() call and js_init_*() function in quickjs-ng's runtime init. Map what depends on what.
2	Extract core-only runtime	Create frost_runtime_create_bare() — a runtime with zero JS stdlib. No console, no Date, no JSON, no setTimeout. Just the VM, GC, and parser.
3	Subsystem headers	Group stdlib functions by domain: frost_std_core.h (Object, Array, JSON), frost_std_io.h (console, print), frost_std_time.h (Date, timers).
4	Registration API	frost_register_std_core(rt), frost_register_std_io(rt), etc. GlacioJS calls these explicitly after frost_runtime_create().
5	Stub unregistered calls	If console isn't registered, console.log throws a clean ReferenceError instead of segfaulting or silently failing.
6	Size audit	Measure binary size difference between full stdlib and bare runtime. Prove modularity has tangible impact.
Deliverables
plain
Copy

libfrostcore.a              // Still one library, but internally split
libfrostcore_bare.a         // (Optional) VM only, for extreme embedding
include/frostcore.h         // Updated: registration functions added
include/frostcore_subsystems.h  // Optional subsystem registry

The Registration API
c
Copy

// After Stage 1: bare runtime
frost_runtime* rt = frost_runtime_create(&alloc);

// Stage 2: GlacioJS chooses what to inject
frost_register_std_core(rt);    // Object, Array, Function, JSON, Math
frost_register_std_io(rt);      // console, print (if any)
frost_register_std_time(rt);    // Date, timers (if quickjs-ng has them)

// GlacioJS native modules come later (Layer 3)
// frost_register_http(rt);
// frost_register_fs(rt);

Explicitly NOT in Stage 2

    ❌ Parser/bytecode modularity (still one compilation unit)
    ❌ GC replacement or algorithm changes
    ❌ Isolate/task scheduler (GlacioJS Layer 2)
    ❌ ES module loader hooks
    ❌ C++ wrapper or embedding API beyond C

Why This Order
Allocator first (Stage 1), then stdlib (Stage 2) because:

    You can't measure per-subsystem memory cost until allocations are tracked
    GlacioJS's philosophy demands "optional subsystem registration" — this makes it real
    It proves the runtime can start minimal and grow capabilities selectively

/*
 * FrostCore — Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JS engine boundary
 * Public C API (Stage 1: Lifecycle + Eval)
 *
 * GlacioJS includes only this header; never includes quickjs.h directly.
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_H
#define FROSTCORE_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Allocator vtable
 *
 * Pass a filled frost_alloc to frost_runtime_create(). Every allocation
 * made by the runtime (including the GC heap) routes through these
 * pointers. userdata is forwarded opaquely on every call — use it for
 * per-isolate arenas, tracing hooks, capacity accounting, etc.
 *
 * calloc is optional: if NULL, the runtime falls back to alloc+memset.
 * malloc_usable_size is optional: if NULL, exact sizes are used instead
 * of the OS slab size, which is slightly less efficient.
 *
 * If alloc is NULL altogether, frost_runtime_create() uses the default
 * system allocator (equivalent to passing malloc/free/realloc).
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr); /* no userdata — POSIX convention */
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Runtime handle — opaque
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Lifecycle
 *
 * frost_runtime_create — alloc may be NULL to use the system allocator.
 *   Returns NULL on allocation failure.
 *
 * frost_runtime_destroy — frees everything owned by this runtime.
 *   Safe to call with NULL (no-op).
 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.
 *
 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Minimal eval surface (integration handshake for GlacioJS)
 *
 * Evaluates `source` as a JS global script expression.
 * Returns  0 on success.
 * Returns -1 on error; *out_error receives a malloc'd (system malloc)
 *   NUL-terminated UTF-8 message — caller must free() it.
 *   out_error may be NULL if the caller doesn't want the message.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_H */

 *   stdlib (Object, Array, Date, JSON, Proxy, Map/Set, TypedArrays,

 *   constructors (Object, Array, …) are visible until registered.

 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.

 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.

frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create_bare(const frost_alloc *alloc);

/*
 * FrostCore — Stage 2: Subsystem Registration API
 *
 * After frost_runtime_create_bare(), GlacioJS selects which JS built-ins
 * to install by calling zero or more frost_register_std_*() functions.
 * Each group is idempotent: calling it twice on the same runtime is safe
 * (returns 0 on the second call, nothing re-installed).
 *
 * Dependency rules (enforced at registration time):
 *   std_collections  requires  std_core
 *   std_async        requires  std_core
 *   std_time         requires  std_core
 *   std_io           requires  std_core   (uses Object, String internally)
 *
 * If a dependency is missing, the register call returns -1 with a
 * descriptive message in *out_error.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   frost_runtime *rt = frost_runtime_create_bare(&alloc);
 *   frost_register_std_core(rt, NULL);
 *   frost_register_std_async(rt, NULL);
 *   // console is intentionally absent — not available in this isolate
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H
#define FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H

#include "frostcore.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Registration return convention (same as frost_eval):
 *   0   success (or already registered — idempotent)
 *  -1   failure; *out_error is malloc'd UTF-8 message, caller must free()
 *       out_error may be NULL.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_core
 *
 * Installs: Object, Function, Array, String, Number, Boolean, Symbol,
 *           Error hierarchy, Iterator, Math, eval(), RegExp, JSON, Proxy,
 *           Map, Set, WeakMap, WeakSet.
 *
 * This is the minimal set for sensible JS execution. Every other
 * subsystem depends on it.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_core(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_collections
 *
 * Installs: TypedArrays (Int8Array … Float64Array, DataView, ArrayBuffer,
 *           SharedArrayBuffer, Atomics), WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_collections(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_async
 *
 * Installs: Promise, async/await support, queueMicrotask,
 *           ArrayBuffer.transfer, atob/btoa, DOMException.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_async(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_time
 *
 * Installs: Date, performance (performance.now / timeOrigin).
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_time(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_io
 *
 * Installs: console.log, print() (global).
 * Output goes to stdout. This is the only subsystem that touches I/O.
 *
 * Requires: std_core
 *
 * Note: This does NOT install the full quickjs-libc module system
 * (no setTimeout, no fs, no os). Those are GlacioJS Layer 3 concerns.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_io(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * frost_register_std_all
 *
 * Convenience: installs all subsystems above in dependency order.
 * Equivalent to frost_runtime_create() but on a bare runtime.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_register_std_all(frost_runtime *rt, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Introspection
 *
 * frost_subsystems_registered — bitmask of what has been registered.
 * Useful for assertions and debug logging in GlacioJS.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
#define FROST_STD_CORE        (1u << 0)
#define FROST_STD_COLLECTIONS (1u << 1)
#define FROST_STD_ASYNC       (1u << 2)
#define FROST_STD_TIME        (1u << 3)
#define FROST_STD_IO          (1u << 4)

unsigned int frost_subsystems_registered(const frost_runtime *rt);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_SUBSYSTEMS_H */

# FrostCore Stage 1+2 — Build System
# Produces:
#   build/libfrostcore.a     — full library (engine + wrapper + subsystems)
#   build/frost_smoke.exe    — Stage 1 smoke test
#   build/frost_subsystems.exe — Stage 2 subsystem test
#
# Usage:
#   make              — build everything, run all tests
#   make lib          — libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         — build + run all tests
#   make size-audit   — print section sizes (lib vs bare estimate)
#   make clean        — remove build/
#
# Variables:
#   CC      — C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      — archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   — output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     — optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage2\"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# quickjs-ng engine (upstream, never modified)
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs-libc.c

# FrostCore boundary layer
FROST_SRCS := \
    src/frostcore.c \
    src/frostcore_subsystems.c

# Test sources
SMOKE_SRCS     := tests/smoke_test.c
SUBSYSTEM_SRCS := tests/subsystem_test.c

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Object files
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_OBJS       := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))
SUBSYSTEM_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SUBSYSTEM_SRCS)))

LIB            := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN      := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke
SUBSYSTEM_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_subsystems

ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN     := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    SUBSYSTEM_BIN := $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN).exe
    LDLIBS        :=
else
    LDLIBS        := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test size-audit clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN) $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 1: Smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 2: Subsystem test ==="
	$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN)

# Binaries
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN): $(SUBSYSTEM_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# Library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# Size audit — llvm-size if available, else size
size-audit: $(LIB)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Size audit: libfrostcore.a ==="
	@command -v llvm-size 2>/dev/null && llvm-size $(LIB) || size $(LIB)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (root include path)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# FrostCore wrapper objects
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/frostcore_subsystems.o: src/frostcore_subsystems.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# Test objects
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/subsystem_test.o: tests/subsystem_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

# FrostCore Stage 1 — Build System
# Produces: build/libfrostcore.a  build/frost_smoke[.exe]
#
# Usage:
#   make              — build lib + smoke test, run test
#   make lib          — libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         — build everything, run smoke test
#   make clean        — remove build/
#
# Variables (override on command line):
#   CC      — C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      — archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   — output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     — optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

# Source root is the parent of this Makefile (the repo root)
ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage1\"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c

FROST_SRCS := src/frostcore.c

SMOKE_SRCS := tests/smoke_test.c

# Object files land in build/
QJS_OBJS   := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))

LIB        := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke

# Detect Windows (MSYS/Git Bash / native) and add .exe suffix
ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    # msvcrt doesn't have -lm but it doesn't need it either
    LDLIBS    :=
else
    LDLIBS    := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Running smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)

# Smoke test binary
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# FrostCore static library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure build dir exists before any .o is built
$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (include path: repo root)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# frostcore wrapper object
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# smoke test object
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# FrostCore Stage 1+2 — Build System
# Produces:
#   build/libfrostcore.a     — full library (engine + wrapper + subsystems)
#   build/frost_smoke.exe    — Stage 1 smoke test
#   build/frost_subsystems.exe — Stage 2 subsystem test
#
# Usage:
#   make              — build everything, run all tests
#   make lib          — libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         — build + run all tests
#   make size-audit   — print section sizes (lib vs bare estimate)
#   make clean        — remove build/
#
# Variables:
#   CC      — C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      — archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   — output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     — optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage2\"

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# quickjs-ng engine (upstream, never modified)
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs-libc.c

# FrostCore boundary layer
FROST_SRCS := \
    src/frostcore.c \
    src/frostcore_subsystems.c

# Test sources
SMOKE_SRCS     := tests/smoke_test.c
SUBSYSTEM_SRCS := tests/subsystem_test.c

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Object files
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_OBJS       := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))
SUBSYSTEM_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SUBSYSTEM_SRCS)))

LIB            := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN      := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke
SUBSYSTEM_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_subsystems

ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN     := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    SUBSYSTEM_BIN := $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN).exe
    LDLIBS        :=
else
    LDLIBS        := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test size-audit clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN) $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 1: Smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 2: Subsystem test ==="
	$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN)

# Binaries
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN): $(SUBSYSTEM_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# Library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# Size audit — llvm-size if available, else size
size-audit: $(LIB)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Size audit: libfrostcore.a ==="
	@command -v llvm-size 2>/dev/null && llvm-size $(LIB) || size $(LIB)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (root include path)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# FrostCore wrapper objects
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/frostcore_subsystems.o: src/frostcore_subsystems.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# Test objects
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/subsystem_test.o: tests/subsystem_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

content.text:
`ctx->eval_internal` is set to `NULL` by default and `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` sets it to `__JS_EvalInternal`. The C-level `JS_Eval()` call hits the `eval is not supported` check when `eval_internal` is NULL — even for `frost_eval()`. So on a bare context, **no JS can be evaluated at all** until `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` is called.

The fix: `frost_runtime_create_bare()` must call `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` (just the eval_internal pointer assignment, zero JS objects) so the VM is usable. This does NOT add `eval()` to the global scope — that's done by `JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects` which adds the `eval` function. `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` only enables the C-level execution path.

Also fix T2: the test strings `"std_core"` need to match the actual error messages which say `"requires std_core"` — this DOES match since `strstr("requires std_core", "std_core")` is true. The failures are purely stderr/stdout ordering. I'll separate them into different streams to confirm, then the real fix is just T1.

That's from a previous run's exit code triggering make's error output — actually it's from the test's own `fprintf` which I changed to `printf` but there's still a `fprintf(stderr, "Some tests FAILED")` at the bottom of `main()`.

**Subsystem groups:**
- `FROST_STD_CORE` (bit 0) — Object, Array, String, Number, Math, eval, RegExp, JSON, Proxy, Map/Set, Symbol, Error hierarchy
- `FROST_STD_COLLECTIONS` (bit 1) — TypedArrays, DataView, ArrayBuffer, WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry
- `FROST_STD_ASYNC` (bit 2) — Promise, atob/btoa, DOMException
- `FROST_STD_TIME` (bit 3) — Date, performance.now/timeOrigin
- `FROST_STD_IO` (bit 4) — console.log, print() global

**Key design decisions:**
- `frost_runtime_create_bare()` calls `JS_NewContextRaw()` + `JS_AddIntrinsicEval()`. The eval intrinsic must be called even on bare runtimes because it sets `ctx->eval_internal` — without it, even the C-level `JS_Eval()` path throws "eval is not supported". It does NOT add a JS `eval` global.
- `frost_register_std_core()` calls `JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects` which adds the JS `eval` global on top.
- `frost_register_std_io()` calls `js_std_add_helpers(ctx, -1, NULL)` — does not pull in the full quickjs-libc module system.
- All registrations are idempotent (bitmask check) and enforce dependency ordering.

### API summary

```c
frost_runtime *rt = frost_runtime_create_bare(&alloc);  // zero stdlib

frost_register_std_core(rt, NULL);        // Object, Array, Math, JSON, RegExp, Map…
frost_register_std_collections(rt, NULL); // TypedArrays, WeakRef
frost_register_std_async(rt, NULL);       // Promise, atob/btoa
frost_register_std_time(rt, NULL);        // Date, performance
frost_register_std_io(rt, NULL);          // console.log, print()
// — or —
frost_register_std_all(rt, NULL);         // all of the above

frost_subsystems_registered(rt);          // → FROST_STD_CORE | FROST_STD_ASYNC | …
```

### Non-obvious fix documented

`frost_runtime_create_bare()` must call `JS_AddIntrinsicEval()` even though it installs nothing visible in JS. Without it, `ctx->eval_internal` stays NULL and every `frost_eval()` call — even `"1+2"` — throws `"eval is not supported"` at the C level. `JS_AddIntrinsicEval` sets the function pointer; `JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects` (inside `frost_register_std_core`) is what puts `eval` into the JS global scope.

content.text: Done. All em dashes replaced with `--` across every FrostCore file — source, headers, Makefile, scripts, and README. The binaries rebuilt clean, still **135 passed, 0 failed**.

Time for Stage 3,
FrostCore Stage 3 — "Parser/Bytecode Boundary"
After memory and stdlib are modular, the next cut is separating the frontend from the backend. quickjs-ng's parser emits bytecode directly into runtime-specific structures. Stage 3 makes the parser a standalone compilation unit that produces a portable intermediate representation the VM can load independently.
Core Tasks
Table
#	Task	What It Means
1	Extract parser state	Remove parser's hidden dependency on JSRuntime internals. Parser should only need: source string, allocator, error callback.
2	Bytecode container	Define frost_bytecode struct — a self-contained blob of opcodes, constants, atom table, and function tables. No runtime pointers.
3	Parse interface	frost_parse(const char* source, frost_bytecode** out, frost_error* err) — source in, bytecode out.
4	Load interface	frost_runtime_load(rt, frost_bytecode* bc) — VM ingests pre-parsed bytecode. Enables parse-once, run-many.
5	Atom table isolation	Parser builds its own atom table during parse. Runtime merges it on load. Breaks the current global atom table assumption.
6	Compilation unit split	Physical separation: frost_parse.c (lexer + parser), frost_bytecode.c (IR format), frost_vm.c (execution engine).
Deliverables
plain
Copy
src/
  frost_alloc.c       // Stage 1
  frost_runtime.c     // Stage 1
  frost_std_*.c       // Stage 2
  frost_parse.c       // Stage 3 (NEW)
  frost_bytecode.c    // Stage 3 (NEW)
  frost_vm.c          // Stage 3 (split from monolith)
include/
  frostcore.h         // Updated with parse/load API
  frost_bytecode.h    // Bytecode IR definition (opaque to GlacioJS)
The API Surface (Stage 3)
c
Copy
// Opaque handle to compiled bytecode
typedef struct frost_bytecode frost_bytecode;

// Parse source into portable bytecode (no runtime needed)
int frost_parse(const char* source, frost_bytecode** out, frost_error* err);

// Load bytecode into a specific runtime for execution
int frost_runtime_load(frost_runtime* rt, frost_bytecode* bc);

// Execute already-loaded bytecode
int frost_runtime_eval_loaded(frost_runtime* rt, frost_bytecode* bc, JSValue* out);

// Destroy bytecode independently of runtime lifecycle
void frost_bytecode_destroy(frost_bytecode* bc);
Explicitly NOT in Stage 3
❌ C++ wrapper or AST exposure (bytecode is the boundary, not AST nodes)
❌ JIT compilation or codegen changes
❌ ES module resolution or loader hooks
❌ GC algorithm changes
❌ Multi-threaded parsing (single-threaded only)
❌ Isolate/task scheduler (still GlacioJS Layer 2)
Why This Order
Allocator → Stdlib → Parser/VM split because:
GlacioJS can now parse JSX (via Yggdrasil) or JS once, cache the bytecode, and inject it into multiple FrostCore runtimes/isolates
The VM becomes smaller — it doesn't need parser tables or lexer state if only running pre-compiled code
It proves the runtime is a true engine that consumes fuel (bytecode), not a monolithic compiler-interpreter
Time Estimate
2–3 weeks
The hard part is decoupling the atom table. quickjs-ng uses a global/runtime-wide atom table for string deduplication and property keys. Making the parser build a local one that gets merged on load requires careful refcount handling.
Let me audit the actual quickjs-ng internals before writing a single line — Stage 3 depends entirely on what's actually entangled.

Perfect! Now I have gathered comprehensive information. Let me compile my findings:

## Thorough Structural Audit: quickjs-ng Codebase

### Q1: Atom Table Architecture

**JSAtom Definition (Line 239):**
```c
typedef struct JSString JSAtomStruct;
```
JSAtom itself is a uint32_t index that references JSAtomStruct in the atom table.

**Atom Table is per-JSRuntime (Lines 275-281):**
```c
struct JSRuntime {
    ...
    int atom_hash_size;           /* power of two */
    int atom_count;
    int atom_size;
    int atom_count_resize;        /* resize hash table at this count */
    uint32_t *atom_hash;          /* hash table */
    JSAtomStruct **atom_array;    /* main atom array */
    int atom_free_index;          /* 0 = none */
    ...
}
```

**Global vs Per-Runtime:** The atom table is **per-JSRuntime**, not global. Each runtime has its own atom_hash (hash table) and atom_array (storage).

**Atom Creation Functions:**
- Line 3358: `JSAtom JS_NewAtomLen(JSContext *ctx, const char *str, size_t len)` - public API
- Line 3376: `JSAtom JS_NewAtom(JSContext *ctx, const char *str)` - public API
- Line 3096: `static JSAtom __JS_NewAtom(JSRuntime *rt, JSString *str, int atom_type)` - internal, takes JSRuntime*

**Atom Lookup:**
- Line 3096-3129: `__JS_NewAtom()` performs lookup via rt->atom_hash and rt->atom_array

**Parser Entry and Atoms:**
- Line 21793: `JSParseState` holds `JSContext *ctx` 
- Parsers call atom functions like `JS_NewAtom(s->ctx, ...)` with JSContext*, which internally extracts rt via `ctx->rt` (line 3035-3045)
- Line 22464: `next_token()` lexer creates atoms directly: `atom = JS_NewAtom(s->ctx, ...)`

### Q2: Parser Entry Points and Signatures

**JS_Eval Signatures (Lines 37494-37509):**
```c
JSValue JS_Eval(JSContext *ctx, const char *input, size_t input_len,
                const char *filename, int eval_flags)

JSValue JS_EvalThis(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj,
                    const char *input, size_t input_len,
                    const char *filename, int eval_flags)

JSValue JS_EvalThis2(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj,
                     const char *input, size_t input_len,
                     JSEvalOptions *options)
```

**Internal Eval (Line 37421):**
```c
static JSValue JS_EvalInternal(JSContext *ctx, JSValueConst this_obj,
                               const char *input, size_t input_len,
                               const char *filename, int line, int flags, int scope_idx)
```

**JSParseState Structure (Lines 21792-21812):**
```c
typedef struct JSParseState {
    JSContext *ctx;               /* directly holds JSContext* */
    int last_line_num, last_col_num, line_num, col_num;
    const char *filename;
    JSToken token;
    bool got_lf;
    const uint8_t *last_ptr, *buf_start, *buf_ptr, *buf_end;
    const uint8_t *eol, *mark;
    JSFunctionDef *cur_func;      /* current function being parsed */
    bool is_module;
    bool allow_html_comments;
} JSParseState;
```

**No intermediate struct:** Parser takes JSContext* directly. JSParseState.ctx points to the JSContext.

**Parser Start (Line 37146):**
```c
static __exception int js_parse_program(JSParseState *s)
```
Called from line 37383 within the eval pipeline.

### Q3: Bytecode Output Format

**JSFunctionBytecode Structure (Lines 779-815):**
```c
typedef struct JSFunctionBytecode {
    JSGCObjectHeader header;
    uint8_t *byte_code_buf;       /* opcode buffer */
    int byte_code_len;
    JSAtom func_name;             /* RUNTIME-RELATIVE INDEX */
    JSVarDef *vardefs;            /* variable definitions (self pointer) */
    JSClosureVar *closure_var;    /* closure variables (self pointer) */
    uint16_t arg_count, var_count, defined_arg_count, stack_size, var_ref_count, closure_var_count;
    int cpool_count;
    JSContext *realm;
    JSValue *cpool;               /* CONSTANT POOL - GC-MANAGED JSValues */
    JSAtom filename;              /* RUNTIME-RELATIVE INDEX */
    int line_num, col_num, source_len;
    int pc2line_len;
    uint8_t *pc2line_buf;
    char *source;
} JSFunctionBytecode;
```

**Contains JSAtom values:** Yes - func_name (line 796) and filename (line 808) are JSAtom indices (runtime-relative)

**Contains JSValue constants:** Yes - cpool (line 807) is `JSValue *cpool` containing GC-managed constant values like nested functions, strings, numbers (line 36248: `memcpy(b->cpool, fd->cpool, b->cpool_count * sizeof(*b->cpool))`)

**Serialization Already Exists:** Yes, fully implemented
- Line 38485: `uint8_t *JS_WriteObject(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags)`
- Line 39765: `JSValue JS_ReadObject(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_len, int flags)`

### Q4: JS_WriteObject / JS_ReadObject

**These functions already exist (public API in quickjs.h):**

**Write Signature (Line 38485):**
```c
uint8_t *JS_WriteObject(JSContext *ctx, size_t *psize, JSValueConst obj, int flags)
```
Returns: self-contained binary blob (DynBuf in BCWriterState line 37660)

**Read Signature (Line 39765):**
```c
JSValue JS_ReadObject(JSContext *ctx, const uint8_t *buf, size_t buf_len, int flags)
```

**Format:** Binary bytecode format with:
- BC_TAG_FUNCTION_BYTECODE (line 37941)
- Atom remapping table (line 37666: `uint32_t *atom_to_idx`)
- Version and checksum (lines 38469-38470)
- Objects and references tables (line 37502-37504 in BCReaderState)

**Runtime-Relative Data Handling:**
- Lines 37751-37789: `bc_atom_to_idx()` remaps atoms from source runtime to serialization indices
- Atoms are serialized via mapping (line 37859: `put_u32(bc_buf + pos + 1, val)` after atom-to-idx conversion)
- Constant pool JSValues are recursively written (line 38005: `JS_WriteObjectRec(s, b->cpool[i])`)

### Q5: Compilation Unit Structure

**Monolithic File:** quickjs.c is entirely self-contained
- No internal `#include "*.c"` includes (verified - none found)
- All 63,419 lines in single file

**Lexer Boundaries (Line 22459):**
```c
static __exception int next_token(JSParseState *s)
```

**Parser Boundaries (Line 37146):**
```c

/*
 * FrostCore -- Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JS engine boundary
 * Public C API (Stage 1+2: Lifecycle, Eval, Subsystem Registration)
 *
 * GlacioJS includes only this header (and optionally frostcore_subsystems.h);
 * never includes quickjs.h directly.
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_H
#define FROSTCORE_H

#include <stddef.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Allocator vtable
 *
 * Pass a filled frost_alloc to frost_runtime_create(). Every allocation
 * made by the runtime (including the GC heap) routes through these
 * pointers. userdata is forwarded opaquely on every call -- use it for
 * per-isolate arenas, tracing hooks, capacity accounting, etc.
 *
 * calloc is optional: if NULL, the runtime falls back to alloc+memset.
 * malloc_usable_size is optional: if NULL, exact sizes are used instead
 * of the OS slab size, which is slightly less efficient.
 *
 * If alloc is NULL altogether, frost_runtime_create() uses the default
 * system allocator (equivalent to passing malloc/free/realloc).
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr); /* no userdata -- POSIX convention */
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Runtime handle -- opaque
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Lifecycle
 *
 * frost_runtime_create -- Full runtime: allocator injection + complete JS
 *   stdlib (Object, Array, Date, JSON, Proxy, Map/Set, TypedArrays,
 *   Promise, WeakRef, RegExp, eval, AToB, Performance). alloc may be
 *   NULL to use the system allocator. Returns NULL on failure.
 *
 * frost_runtime_create_bare -- Same allocator injection, but the JS
 *   context has ZERO stdlib installed. GlacioJS must call
 *   frost_register_std_*() to add only the subsystems it needs.
 *   Even typeof, throw, etc. work -- the VM runs -- but no global
 *   constructors (Object, Array, …) are visible until registered.
 *
 * frost_runtime_destroy -- frees everything. Safe to call with NULL.
 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.
 *
 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create_bare(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Minimal eval surface (integration handshake for GlacioJS)
 *
 * Evaluates `source` as a JS global script expression.
 * Returns  0 on success.
 * Returns -1 on error; *out_error receives a malloc'd (system malloc)
 *   NUL-terminated UTF-8 message -- caller must free() it.
 *   out_error may be NULL if the caller doesn't want the message.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_H */

- **Stage 2**: Subsystem split — `frost_runtime_create_bare()` + `frost_register_std_*()` registration API with bitmask tracking, dependency enforcement, idempotency, and a 135-test suite.
- **Stage 3** (in progress): Parser/Bytecode boundary — `frost_parse()` (compile-only, produces portable blob), `frost_bytecode_destroy()`, `frost_runtime_load()`, `frost_runtime_eval_loaded()`. User explicitly requested "add appropriate tests."

   - `JSMallocFunctions` opaque arg order: `(opaque, size, ...)` vs `frost_alloc` userdata-last — bridged with static thunk functions
   - `JS_NewContextRaw()`: installs only VM bootstrap, no JS globals — used for bare runtime
   - `JS_AddIntrinsicEval()`: sets `ctx->eval_internal` function pointer; MUST be called even on bare runtimes or `JS_Eval()` at C level throws "eval is not supported"
   - `JS_AddIntrinsicBaseObjects()`: installs Object/Array/Math/etc and also adds JS `eval` global
   - `js_std_add_helpers()`: installs `console.log` + `print()` from quickjs-libc
   - `JS_EVAL_FLAG_COMPILE_ONLY`: compiles source without executing, returns function JSValue
   - `JS_WriteObject` / `JS_ReadObject`: serialize/deserialize function bytecode to self-contained binary blob with atom remapping — already fully implemented in quickjs-ng
   - `JS_EvalFunction()`: executes a deserialized function object
   - Per-runtime atom table: `rt->atom_hash` / `rt->atom_array` — atoms are runtime-relative uint32_t indices
   - Physical parser/VM split not feasible: codegen is interleaved with parsing in the monolith
   - `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` + `_WINSOCKAPI_`: required to compile `quickjs-libc.c` with clang on Windows
   - Bitmask subsystem tracking: `FROST_STD_CORE (1<<0)`, `FROST_STD_COLLECTIONS (1<<1)`, `FROST_STD_ASYNC (1<<2)`, `FROST_STD_TIME (1<<3)`, `FROST_STD_IO (1<<4)`

/*
 * FrostCore -- Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JS engine boundary
 * Public C API (Stage 1+2+3: Lifecycle, Eval, Subsystem Registration,
 *               Bytecode Parse/Load)
 *
 * GlacioJS includes only this header (and optionally frostcore_subsystems.h
 * and frost_bytecode.h); never includes quickjs.h directly.
 */
#ifndef FROSTCORE_H
#define FROSTCORE_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include "frost_bytecode.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Allocator vtable
 *
 * Pass a filled frost_alloc to frost_runtime_create(). Every allocation
 * made by the runtime (including the GC heap) routes through these
 * pointers. userdata is forwarded opaquely on every call -- use it for
 * per-isolate arenas, tracing hooks, capacity accounting, etc.
 *
 * calloc is optional: if NULL, the runtime falls back to alloc+memset.
 * malloc_usable_size is optional: if NULL, exact sizes are used instead
 * of the OS slab size, which is slightly less efficient.
 *
 * If alloc is NULL altogether, frost_runtime_create() uses the default
 * system allocator (equivalent to passing malloc/free/realloc).
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr); /* no userdata -- POSIX convention */
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Runtime handle -- opaque
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
typedef struct frost_runtime frost_runtime;

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Lifecycle
 *
 * frost_runtime_create -- Full runtime: allocator injection + complete JS
 *   stdlib (Object, Array, Date, JSON, Proxy, Map/Set, TypedArrays,
 *   Promise, WeakRef, RegExp, eval, AToB, Performance). alloc may be
 *   NULL to use the system allocator. Returns NULL on failure.
 *
 * frost_runtime_create_bare -- Same allocator injection, but the JS
 *   context has ZERO stdlib installed. GlacioJS must call
 *   frost_register_std_*() to add only the subsystems it needs.
 *   Even typeof, throw, etc. work -- the VM runs -- but no global
 *   constructors (Object, Array, ...) are visible until registered.
 *
 * frost_runtime_destroy -- frees everything. Safe to call with NULL.
 *   The runtime is NOT usable after this call.
 *
 * Multiple runtimes may coexist in the same process without sharing
 * any mutable state.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create_bare(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Stage 1: Minimal eval surface
 *
 * Evaluates `source` as a JS global script in one shot.
 * Returns  0 on success.
 * Returns -1 on error; *out_error receives a malloc'd (system malloc)
 *   NUL-terminated UTF-8 message -- caller must free() it.
 *   out_error may be NULL.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);

/* -----------------------------------------------------------------------
 * Stage 3: Parser / Bytecode boundary
 *
 * frost_parse
 *   Compiles `source` to a portable bytecode blob. No runtime is needed;
 *   a temporary scratch runtime is created and destroyed internally.
 *   The resulting frost_bytecode* is independent of any runtime lifecycle.
 *
 *   source    -- NUL-terminated JS source text
 *   filename  -- used in error messages / stack traces; may be NULL
 *   out       -- receives the frost_bytecode* on success
 *   err       -- receives error details on failure; fields are 0/NULL on
 *                success. May be NULL if caller doesn't want diagnostics.
 *
 *   Returns  0 on success.
 *   Returns -1 on syntax/compile error; *out is NULL, err filled.
 *
 * frost_bytecode_destroy
 *   Frees the bytecode blob. Safe to call with NULL.
 *   Independent of any runtime -- does not require the runtime that
 *   parsed or loaded it to still be alive.
 *
 * frost_runtime_load
 *   Deserialises a frost_bytecode into a runtime, making it ready to
 *   execute. The same bytecode blob may be loaded into multiple runtimes
 *   simultaneously (parse-once, run-many). Does NOT execute the code.
 *
 *   Returns  0 on success.
 *   Returns -1 on error (e.g. incompatible bytecode version, OOM);
 *            *out_error is malloc'd -- caller must free(). May be NULL.
 *
 * frost_runtime_eval_loaded
 *   Executes a previously loaded bytecode object inside `rt`.
 *   Must be called after frost_runtime_load() on the same runtime.
 *   The same loaded_bc may be executed multiple times (run-many).
 *
 *   loaded_bc -- the frost_bytecode* that was passed to frost_runtime_load
 *   Returns  0 on success.
 *   Returns -1 on JS runtime error; *out_error is malloc'd. May be NULL.
 * ----------------------------------------------------------------------- */
int  frost_parse(const char *source, const char *filename,
                 frost_bytecode **out, frost_error *err);

void frost_bytecode_destroy(frost_bytecode *bc);

int  frost_runtime_load(frost_runtime *rt, const frost_bytecode *bc,
                        char **out_error);

int  frost_runtime_eval_loaded(frost_runtime *rt, const frost_bytecode *bc,
                               char **out_error);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* FROSTCORE_H */

# FrostCore Stage 1 -- Windows build + smoke test
# Usage: .\build.ps1 [-BuildType Debug|Release]
param(
    [string]$BuildType = "Release"
)
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$opt = if ($BuildType -eq "Debug") { "-O0 -g" } else { "-O2" }

Write-Host "=== FrostCore build ($BuildType) ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# Locate clang and llvm-ar
$clang  = (Get-Command clang  -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)?.Source ?? "clang"
$llvmar = (Get-Command llvm-ar -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)?.Source ?? "ar"

# make.exe from Git for Windows or GnuWin32
$make = (Get-Command make -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)?.Source
if (-not $make) { throw "make not found -- install Git for Windows or GnuWin32" }

& $make -C frost `
    "CC=$clang" `
    "AR=$llvmar" `
    "OPT=$opt" `
    "BUILD=build"

if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Build failed" }

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "=== Artifacts ===" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Get-Item "frost\build\libfrostcore.a","frost\build\libfrostcore.lib" `
    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, Length

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Build complete." -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  frost\build\libfrostcore.a  -- link into GlacioJS"
Write-Host "  frost\include\frostcore.h   -- include in GlacioJS"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# FrostCore Stage 1 -- Unix build + smoke test
# Usage: ./build.sh [Debug|Release]
set -euo pipefail

BUILD_TYPE="${1:-Release}"

if [ "$BUILD_TYPE" = "Debug" ]; then
    OPT="-O0 -g"
else
    OPT="-O2"
fi

echo "=== FrostCore build (${BUILD_TYPE}) ==="

# Prefer clang, fall back to cc
CC="${CC:-$(command -v clang || echo cc)}"
AR="${AR:-$(command -v llvm-ar || command -v ar)}"

make -C frost \
    CC="$CC" \
    AR="$AR" \
    OPT="$OPT" \
    BUILD=build

echo ""
echo "=== Artifacts ==="
ls -lh frost/build/libfrostcore.a

echo ""
echo "Build complete."
echo "  frost/build/libfrostcore.a   -- link into GlacioJS"
echo "  frost/include/frostcore.h    -- include in GlacioJS"

# FrostCore Stage 1+2+3 -- Build System
# Produces:
#   build/libfrostcore.a       -- full library (engine + wrapper + subsystems + bytecode)
#   build/frost_smoke.exe      -- Stage 1 smoke test
#   build/frost_subsystems.exe -- Stage 2 subsystem test
#   build/frost_bytecode.exe   -- Stage 3 bytecode test
#
# Usage:
#   make              -- build everything, run all tests
#   make lib          -- libfrostcore.a only
#   make test         -- build + run all tests
#   make size-audit   -- print section sizes (lib vs bare estimate)
#   make clean        -- remove build/
#
# Variables:
#   CC      -- C compiler          (default: clang)
#   AR      -- archiver            (default: llvm-ar, falls back to ar)
#   BUILD   -- output directory    (default: build)
#   OPT     -- optimisation flags  (default: -O2)

CC      ?= clang
AR      ?= $(shell command -v llvm-ar 2>/dev/null || echo ar)
BUILD   ?= build
OPT     ?= -O2

ROOT    := ..

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Flags
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
CFLAGS := \
    -std=c11 \
    $(OPT) \
    -Wall \
    -Wextra \
    -Wno-unused-parameter \
    -Wno-sign-compare \
    -Wno-missing-field-initializers \
    -D_GNU_SOURCE \
    -DCONFIG_VERSION=\"frostcore-stage3\" \
    -DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN \
    -D_WINSOCKAPI_

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source lists
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

# quickjs-ng engine (upstream, never modified)
QJS_SRCS := \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs.c \
    $(ROOT)/libregexp.c \
    $(ROOT)/libunicode.c \
    $(ROOT)/dtoa.c \
    $(ROOT)/quickjs-libc.c

# FrostCore boundary layer
FROST_SRCS := \
    src/frostcore.c \
    src/frostcore_subsystems.c \
    src/frost_parse.c \
    src/frost_vm.c

# Test sources
SMOKE_SRCS     := tests/smoke_test.c
SUBSYSTEM_SRCS := tests/subsystem_test.c
BYTECODE_SRCS  := tests/bytecode_test.c

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Object files
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
QJS_OBJS       := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(QJS_SRCS)))
FROST_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(FROST_SRCS)))
SMOKE_OBJS     := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SMOKE_SRCS)))
SUBSYSTEM_OBJS := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(SUBSYSTEM_SRCS)))
BYTECODE_OBJS  := $(patsubst %.c,$(BUILD)/%.o,$(notdir $(BYTECODE_SRCS)))

LIB            := $(BUILD)/libfrostcore.a
SMOKE_BIN      := $(BUILD)/frost_smoke
SUBSYSTEM_BIN  := $(BUILD)/frost_subsystems
BYTECODE_BIN   := $(BUILD)/frost_bytecode

ifeq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
    SMOKE_BIN     := $(SMOKE_BIN).exe
    SUBSYSTEM_BIN := $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN).exe
    BYTECODE_BIN  := $(BYTECODE_BIN).exe
    LDLIBS        :=
else
    LDLIBS        := -lm
endif

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Targets
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
.PHONY: all lib test size-audit clean

all: test

lib: $(LIB)

test: $(SMOKE_BIN) $(SUBSYSTEM_BIN) $(BYTECODE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 1: Smoke test ==="
	$(SMOKE_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 2: Subsystem test ==="
	$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Stage 3: Bytecode test ==="
	$(BYTECODE_BIN)

# Binaries
$(SMOKE_BIN): $(SMOKE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(SUBSYSTEM_BIN): $(SUBSYSTEM_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

$(BYTECODE_BIN): $(BYTECODE_OBJS) $(LIB)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $^ $(LDLIBS)

# Library
$(LIB): $(FROST_OBJS) $(QJS_OBJS)
	$(AR) rcs $@ $^

# Size audit -- llvm-size if available, else size
size-audit: $(LIB)
	@echo ""
	@echo "=== Size audit: libfrostcore.a ==="
	@command -v llvm-size 2>/dev/null && llvm-size $(LIB) || size $(LIB)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compilation rules
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

$(BUILD):
	mkdir -p $(BUILD)

# quickjs-ng engine objects (root include path)
$(BUILD)/%.o: $(ROOT)/%.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -c -o $@ $<

# FrostCore wrapper objects
$(BUILD)/frostcore.o: src/frostcore.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/frostcore_subsystems.o: src/frostcore_subsystems.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -I$(ROOT) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# Test objects
$(BUILD)/smoke_test.o: tests/smoke_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

$(BUILD)/subsystem_test.o: tests/subsystem_test.c | $(BUILD)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -Iinclude -c -o $@ $<

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

# FrostCore

**Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JavaScript engine boundary layer.**

FrostCore wraps [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) with a thin C API that gives the embedding layer -- GlacioJS -- explicit control over memory allocation, runtime lifecycle, and JS evaluation. It is not a rewrite of the engine; it is an extraction boundary on top of a living upstream codebase.

---

## What FrostCore Is

| Capability | Status |
|---|---|
| Per-runtime pluggable allocator | Stage 1 |
| Explicit `create` / `destroy` lifecycle (no hidden globals) | Stage 1 |
| Multiple runtimes coexisting in one process | Stage 1 |
| Minimal `eval` surface for integration testing | Stage 1 |
| GC algorithm changes | Not in scope |
| Parser/bytecode modularization | Stage 3+ |
| Stdlib separation | Stage 3+ |
| C++ wrapper | Not in scope |
| Task/isolate scheduler | GlacioJS Layer 2 |

---

## Repository Layout

```
FrostCore/
  quickjs.c / quickjs.h    -- upstream quickjs-ng engine (do not edit)
  libregexp.c / libunicode.c / dtoa.c -- upstream support files
  CMakeLists.txt / meson.build        -- upstream build (untouched)
  README.txt                          -- original quickjs-ng README

  frost/                   -- FrostCore overlay (all Stage 1 work lives here)
    include/frostcore.h    -- public C API -- the ONLY header GlacioJS imports
    src/frostcore.c        -- implementation
    tests/smoke_test.c     -- isolation + leak smoke test
    Makefile               -- builds libfrostcore.a without CMake

  build.sh                 -- Unix: build + run smoke test
  build.ps1                -- Windows: build + run smoke test
```

---

## Public API (Stage 1)

```c
#include "frostcore.h"

/* Allocator vtable -- all fields except alloc/free/realloc are optional */
typedef struct frost_alloc {
    void *(*calloc)(size_t count, size_t size, void *userdata);
    void *(*alloc)(size_t size, void *userdata);
    void  (*free)(void *ptr, void *userdata);
    void *(*realloc)(void *ptr, size_t size, void *userdata);
    size_t (*malloc_usable_size)(const void *ptr);
    void  *userdata;
} frost_alloc;

/* Pass NULL to use the system allocator */
frost_runtime *frost_runtime_create(const frost_alloc *alloc);
void           frost_runtime_destroy(frost_runtime *rt);

/* Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
   *out_error is malloc'd -- caller must free() it. */
int frost_eval(frost_runtime *rt, const char *source, char **out_error);
```

---

## Building

### Unix (clang required)

```sh
chmod +x build.sh
./build.sh          # Release
./build.sh Debug
```

Produces `frost/build/libfrostcore.a` and runs the smoke test.

### Windows (PowerShell, clang in PATH)

```powershell
.\build.ps1
.\build.ps1 -BuildType Debug
```

Produces `frost\build\frostcore.lib` and runs the smoke test.

### Manual (from `frost/`)

```sh
make              # builds libfrostcore.a + smoke test, runs test
make lib          # libfrostcore.a only
make clean
```

---

## Smoke Test Output (Stage 1)

```
FrostCore Stage 1 -- Smoke Test
================================
[rt_sys]   Creating runtime with system allocator...
[rt_count] Creating runtime with counting allocator...
[rt_sys2]  Creating second system-allocator runtime...

All three runtimes created successfully.

--- Eval tests ---
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval(1 + 1) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval(Math.sqrt(144)) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys]:   eval('hello' + ' world') => ok
  PASS [rt_count]: eval(42 * 2) => ok
  PASS [rt_count]: eval(typeof undefined) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys2]:  eval(true || false) => ok
  PASS [rt_sys2]:  eval([1,2,3].length) => ok

--- Error handling ---
  PASS [rt_sys/syntax]:  SyntaxError: expecting ';'
  PASS [rt_count/ref]:   ReferenceError: undeclaredVariable is not defined
  PASS [rt_sys2/throw]:  Error: boom

--- Isolation test ---
  PASS [isolation]: __SENTINEL__ not visible in rt_sys2

--- Allocator accounting ---
  rt_count stats after destroy: allocs=1246, frees=1246   ← zero leaks

================================
All smoke tests PASSED.
```

---

## Upstream

FrostCore is built on [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) (MIT).
The original quickjs-ng README is preserved in [README.txt](README.txt).

Upstream sync strategy: `master` tracks `quickjs-ng/master`. All FrostCore work lives in `frost/` and never modifies upstream files, making rebases clean.

**Allocator-injectable, multi-runtime JavaScript engine boundary layer.**

FrostCore wraps [quickjs-ng](https://github.com/quickjs-ng/quickjs) with a thin C API that gives the embedding layer -- GlacioJS -- explicit control over memory allocation, runtime lifecycle, subsystem registration, and bytecode compilation. ---

## What FrostCore Is

| Capability | Status |

| Subsystem dependency enforcement and idempotency | Stage 2 |

| C++ wrapper | Not in scope |
